title: Operator bridge scripts and public templates
summary: Practical quick-guide for on-call operators to run an incident bridge and produce customer-facing status updates. Includes short scripts, status page templates, internal war-room checklist, escalation ladder, and suggested timing/cadence for communications. Designed to be used in high-pressure outages where clear, consistent messaging and minimal cognitive load are essential.
audience: Bridge leads, on-call SREs, incident commanders, support leads, customer success on-call
purpose: Reduce friction in incident communications by providing pre-baked, editable scripts and a minimal checklist that operators can copy/paste into Slack, Statuspage, email, or support tickets. Prioritize: safety (avoid revealing PII/security), accuracy, and timeliness.
scope: Covers: triage-to-stable incident bridges, public status page messages across three visibility levels (investigating, degraded, identifying root cause, mitigated), customer-facing templates for enterprise and SMB, internal update cadence, and an operator war-room checklist. Not a full postmortem template.
operational-principles: 1) One truth: pick one source (bridge lead) for public messaging. 2) Timebox initial public message to <=15 minutes after detection if customer impact is verified. 3) Err on the side of transparency (impact, affected features, initial mitigation steps) but never speculate on root cause. 4) Use consistent severity language: Investigating, Degraded, Partial Outage, Major Outage, Mitigated. 5) Link to a central incident doc or timeline for follow-ups.
war-room-checklist: 1. Bridge creation: create a private bridge channel (Zoom/Hangouts/Signal) and a public Slack incident thread. 2. Roles: assign Bridge Lead, Scribe, Communications Lead, Triage Engineer, Escalation POC. 3. Capture initial facts: detection time, first alert or customer report, affected services, initial error metrics (5m/1m error rate, latency, capacity). 4. Initial public statement: post an 'Investigating' message to Statuspage and public channel (see templates below). 5. Short cadence: 15m updates for first hour, then every 30m until degraded/mitigated. 6. Mitigations: document quick workarounds and rollbacks. 7. Escalate to on-call leader or pager duty when threshold crossed (impact > X customers or significant revenue impact). 8. When service recovers: publish 'Mitigated' update with next steps and PM/PT owner for postmortem. 9. Post-bridge checklist: ensure status page closure, ticket routing, and postmortem assigned within 72 hours.
ops-roles-and-responsibilities: Bridge Lead: single voice for public updates. Scribe: live note taker and timeline maintainer. Communications Lead: crafts customer-facing language and coordinates CS. Triage Engineer: reproduces/isolates fault and runs mitigation. Escalation POC: coordination with on-call manager and exec notification as needed.
escalation-ladder: Level 1: On-call engineer -> Level 2: Senior on-call / Team lead -> Level 3: Eng manager or SRE manager -> Level 4: Director of Platform/On-call Director. If customer contracts or enterprise SLAs are at risk, notify Customer Success (CS rep) and Escalation Manager immediately.
decision-matrix: If impact limited to internal monitoring with negligible customer facing errors: internal triage, no statuspage update. If any customer-facing errors or API timeouts observed for >5 minutes across >1% of requests: post 'Investigating' and escalate bridge. If key features completely unavailable for >15 minutes or revenue/SLAs impacted: classify as Major Outage and notify execs.
communication-cadence: Initial: within 15 minutes of verified customer impact. Rapid updates: every 15 minutes for first 60 minutes. Stabilization cadence: every 30 minutes until mitigated. Final: post-mitigation summary within 2 hours of recovery, postmortem assignment within 72 hours.
statuspage-templates:
-- STATUSPAGE TEMPLATE: INVESTIGATING (short) --
Title: Investigating: degraded responses from Redwood API
Impact: Some customers may experience increased latency or failed requests to text-generation endpoints.
What we're doing: We're currently investigating the issue and assessing scope. We'll post updates every 15 minutes.
Next update: in ~15 minutes or sooner.
Link: [private incident doc link]
-- END --

-- STATUSPAGE TEMPLATE: PARTIAL SERVICE DEGRADATION (detailed) --
Title: Partial degradation: embeddings and generation endpoints affected
Impact: A subset of requests to embeddings and text-generation endpoints may time out or return errors. This affects some customers in us-west-2 and eu-west-1.
Scope: Estimated 3% of requests. Enterprise tenants are intermittently affected.
What we're doing: We've opened an incident and have a bridge. Engineers are investigating routing and GPU node health. We're applying mitigations (traffic reroute, scaling additional workers).
Workaround: Retry requests with exponential backoff; prioritize critical requests.
Next update: in 15 minutes.
-- END --

-- STATUSPAGE TEMPLATE: MITIGATED --
Title: Service restored: API latency and errors mitigated
Impact: The issue affecting generation and embeddings endpoints has been mitigated. Services returned to normal at 15:42 UTC.
What we did: We identified a strain in the routing layer caused by unhealthy worker churn and applied a temporary reroute and increased pool size. A full root cause analysis is in progress.
Next steps: Full postmortem shared within 72 hours. If you continue to see issues, contact support@redwoodinference.com.
-- END --
customer-email-templates:
-- CUSTOMER (ENTERPRISE) INITIAL EMAIL --
Subject: Incident: degraded API responses – investigating (Redwood Inference)
Hi <Customer Name>,
We’re reaching out to let you know we are currently investigating an issue affecting API responses for some customers. You may see increased latency or occasional errors. Our engineering team is actively working on a fix from our incident bridge.
Impact: Intermittent API errors and higher latency for a subset of requests.
What we are doing: We’ve opened an incident, created a bridge, and are actively investigating both routing and worker health.
ETA for next update: ~15 minutes. We will update via status page and this thread.
If this issue is causing severe disruption to your production systems, please reply with urgency and we will escalate.
Thanks for your patience,
Claire Nguyen
SRE, Redwood Inference
-- END --

-- CUSTOMER (SMB) PUBLIC SMS/SLACK OR IN-APP NOTICE --
We’re aware that some requests to the Redwood API are failing or slow. Our engineers are working on a fix. Check status.redwood.ai for updates or contact support. We’ll post another update shortly.
-- END --
internal-bridge-scripts-and-slack-posts:
Initial Slack post (internal incident channel):

:rotating_light: Incident created – Bridge Lead @<name> (start 14:02 UTC)
Summary: Investigating increased 5xx rate and high tail latency for /v1/generate in us-west-2.
Actions: Bridge created, scribe assigned, triage engineer reproducing.
First public update: posted to statuspage at 14:10 UTC.
Cadence: 15m updates.

Bridge update template (internal):
Time: 14:27 UTC
State: Investigating / Partial degradation
Facts gathered: error spike started at 14:00 UTC, 5xx rate peaked at 7% at 14:11 UTC, GPU worker churn observed in us-west-2.
Actions taken: scaled pool +3 workers, rerouted traffic away from unhealthy hosts, core-engineer running heap checks.

-- END --
mitigation-playbooks-summary: Common mitigations to try (fast, low-risk first): 1) Reroute traffic away from affected AZ/region. 2) Increase worker pool or enable burst capacity. 3) Toggle fallback model variant (lower memory/quantized) for heavy routes. 4) Restart suspect GPU nodes with drain/restart flow. 5) Revert last deploy if incident coincides with recent rollout. Document each action and time in the timeline.
customer-faq-and-talking-points:
Q: Is my data safe? A: Yes — no evidence of data exfiltration. We never surface PII in status updates.
Q: When will this be fixed? A: We are actively mitigating; we’ll post updates on the cadence above. We avoid promising an ETA until we have a mitigation.
Q: Do you have a workaround? A: Use retry with backoff, reduce max tokens or request smaller batch sizes, or temporarily use alternative endpoints/regions.
Q: Will this affect billing? A: We will evaluate impact and provide credits per our SLA for qualifying incidents after the postmortem process.
post-incident-handoff: When incident is closed: 1) Bridge Lead posts final Mitigated status on statuspage and internal channel. 2) Scribe extracts timeline and uploads to incident doc. 3) Triage owner files a postmortem issue and assigns an author within 72 hours. 4) Communications Lead drafts customer incident summary and shares to CS. 5) Operations schedules remediation tickets for hard fixes.
quick-copy-clipboard-friendly-snippets:
Copyable: 'We’re investigating increased errors/latency affecting some API requests. Engineers are on it — next update ~15 minutes.'
Copyable (exec alert): 'Major outage detected affecting core API; immediate attention from platform leadership recommended. See incident bridge: <link>.'
Copyable (close): 'Services restored. We will follow with a postmortem in 72 hours.'
safety-and-compliance-notes: Do NOT include customer-identifiable info or internal hostnames on public status pages. Redact or avoid specific API keys, internal ticket numbers, or memory addresses in public messages. If a security incident is suspected, follow the security incident runbook and notify secops immediately instead of public status messaging.
examples-and-lessons-learned: Example: 2025-08-21 burst worker churn – initial investigating message posted at 10:03 UTC; mitigation (traffic reroute) applied at 10:10 UTC; full mitigation at 10:25 UTC. Lesson: autoscaler threshold was too sensitive to short IO spikes. Action: adjust scale-down cooldowns and add health-check delays.
next-steps-for-document: 1) Iterate with CS on enterprise email tone options. 2) Add a short checklist card to the on-call runbook for mobile responders. 3) Convert top 3 templates into Slack snippets and Statuspage macros. 4) Run a comms wargame next quarter to validate cadence and roles.

notes: This doc is intentionally concise and copy-paste friendly. Keep updates short, factual, and consistent. Replace placeholders before posting and confirm timezones (UTC always on status pages).
